Italy was not West Frankish: Lothair II's heir in 869 was 'his brother, Emperor Louis II of Italy' (Meerssen page), who held it until his death in 875. The Italian block is removed. The Breton cells are already out here. Cliopatria has no Kingdom of Italy shape for 845-886; the kingdom-of-italy dossier (eu-13) must cover those years. Repair of 2026-10-24: of the 58 added cells that are not Italy, 33 are Corsica and 7 Alpine or Hainaut cells that Cliopatria takes from its Middle Franks row (Lothair I's realm) together with Italy, 18 are Gironde and Basque-coast cells (West Frankish fill, kept) and one is the San Marino cell. Corsica and the San Marino cell are now removed with the Italian block in the seven corrections of 860-880; the History of Corsica page has Charlemagne conquering it in 774 and the Carolingian Empire fighting the Saracens for it, and puts it under no West Frankish king. The 7 Alpine cells (Ticino, Graubünden, Aosta side) stay: no page.

887 (one year), 1,591 cells (402,364 km2 by cell count; Cliopatria table 380,144): France and Belgium, with Aquitaine. Charles the Fat is deposed by 17 November 887; the realms 'each elected a kinglet'. The page gives no area. Boso's realm is Louis the Blind's again (May 887, ledger).

888-895, 750 cells (189,675 km2): Odo's kingdom north of the Loire, 'Margrave of Neustria' with Paris, 'rarely outside of Northern France'. Ranulf II of Aquitaine declared himself king in 888 and 'submitted by 889' (Odo page), so Aquitaine (843 cells) is a vassal (ledger) and left out of the base shape. The page says Odo 'definitively' separated West Francia from the Carolingian Empire; it gives no borders. From 896 Cliopatria's own West Franks shape holds Aquitaine again (see west-franks_896).

896-897, 1,572 cells: Cliopatria puts Aquitaine (824 cells) into the West Franks the year its own Aquitaine row ends, and the shape is kept as drawn. Repair of 2026-10-24: the first version subtracted Cliopatria's whole Aquitaine 895 shape, but that shape is all of southern France (Toulouse 13 cells, Narbonne 8, Bordeaux 11, Auvergne), not only the duchy that the West Francia page says 'was largely outside the control of the West Frankish kings', and no dossier owns the removed land in 896-989. The Odo page: Odo 'was still the last ruler of West Francia for three centuries to take any interest in Aquitaine'. Aquitaine (Toulouse, Septimania, Gascony, Bordeaux and Auvergne, 844 cells in Cliopatria's Aquitaine 895 shape) stays inside the base shape as nominal West Frankish sovereignty; the level of control is the vassal pair of the ledger (889-989, tint). Odo agrees in 896 'to cede part of the realm' to Charles, who held only Laon in 897 (Charles the Simple page).

898-910, 1,573 cells: as 896 with one Septimania cell added by Cliopatria (no page). Charles the Simple succeeds Odo in January 898; the base shape is Cliopatria's, as in 896 (he 'was placed under Ranulf II, Duke of Aquitaine', who 'used the royal title himself until making peace with Odo'). Aquitaine (Toulouse, Septimania, Gascony, Bordeaux and Auvergne, 844 cells in Cliopatria's Aquitaine 895 shape) stays inside the base shape as nominal West Frankish sovereignty; the level of control is the vassal pair of the ledger (889-989, tint).

911-921, 2,074 cells (491,031 km2): right in adding Lotharingia (538 cells; Lotharingian nobles 'declared Charles their new king, breaking from East Francia'; crowned in early November 911) and in taking 37 Norman cells off for Rollo ('all the land between the river Epte and the sea', autumn 911). Aquitaine is inside the shape, as in 896.

Cliopatria's Urgell grows by 42 cells in 878 (24 in Barcelona province, 17 in Girona province), which fit; Cliopatria's own rows for Barcelona and Besalú begin only in 898, so the counterpart stays county-of-urgell and county-of-barcelona and county-of-besalu are the later owners. 'They elected Boso king and successor to Louis the Stammerer' at the Synod of Mantaille, 15 October 879; the Ribemont page: Boso 'proclaimed himself king and seized power in Lower Burgundy and Provence'. 'After Louis and Carloman divided their father's realm at Amiens in March 880, the two brothers joined to march against Boso. They took Mâcon and the northern parts of Boso's realm.' The capture is undated on the page (after March 880), so no month is given; the page names Mâcon only and the region is the Saône-et-Loire reading.

region.text: western Lotharingia, which Cliopatria moves to the East Franks in 880

region.text: Boso's realm except the county of Vienne

region.text: Provence and Lower Burgundy

Boso's realm leaves the Carolingian crown.

region.text: Aquitaine under Ranulf II

ledger.note: 888: Aquitaine breaks away. After Charles the Fat's fall 'Ranulf II declared himself king' in Aquitaine; the page is unsure whether this followed his deposition (November 887) or death (13 January 888). Cliopatria's Aquitaine row begins in 888.

888: Odo, a Robertian, is crowned king at Compiègne. 'He was crowned at Compiègne in February 888 by Walter, Archbishop of Sens'; the page: his reign 'marked the definitive separation of West Francia from the Carolingian Empire'. Carolingian rule ends; colour and dossier continue.

region.text: Aquitaine, the name the West Francia page uses ('Aquitania, Guyenne and Gascony' in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 889: Ranulf of Aquitaine submits to Odo. 'Ranulf (or Ramnulf) of Aquitaine submitted by 889.' The West Francia page adds that Aquitaine 'was largely outside the control of the West Frankish kings', so it is a vassal (tint), not a province. Lothair of France page: in 982 Louis was 'crowned King and Queen of Aquitaine' at Vieille-Brioude; Duchy of Aquitaine page: the dukes were subordinate in principle 'despite disagreement with their Frankish overlords' and Charles the Simple 'bestowed the duchy upon William the Pious' in 893. The region is the gazetteer's Aquitaine, because the pages do not separate Toulouse or Gascony; the land is inside the base shape and the tint marks the level of control. The counterpart is the slug that must own the duchy in 896-989 (Cliopatria's Duchy of Aquitaine begins in 990).

region.text: Cliopatria's Aquitaine 895 shape, which its West Franks shape holds from 896

ledger.note: 896: Cliopatria's West Franks shape takes in Aquitaine (824 cells) the year its own Aquitaine row ends. No opened page records an annexation: the West Francia page says Aquitaine 'was largely outside the control of the West Frankish kings' and the Odo page that Ranulf 'submitted by 889'. The event marks a change of drawing, not a conquest; the land is a vassal (tint) through the pair 889-989.
898: the Carolingians return. 'Odo died in La Fère on 1 January 898, succeeded by Charles' (the Simple), who had been crowned a rival king at Reims in 893.

region.text: Rouen and the area of present-day Upper Normandy, west of the Epte

ledger.note: 911: Rollo receives the land around Rouen. The treaty date is 'likely in the autumn of 911'; Charles 'offered him the land west of the river Epte'; 'the consensus is that it was broadly Rouen and the area of present-day Upper Normandy'; Rollo 'agreed to be baptised and pledged vassalage'. Cliopatria shows the land as Viking settlements until its Duchy of Normandy begins in 922.

minus.text: the East Frankish kingdom's own lands before 925 (Westphalia east of the Rhine, the Worms-Speyer-Mainz Rhine Franconia); its German cells only (the shape also covers 18 cells of Drenthe, Overijssel and Gelderland, which stay Lotharingian: 'the Netherlands')

region.text: the Lotharingian duchy under Reginar, less the East Frankish lands of 922 east of the Rhine (the gazetteer region Lotharingia is all of Nordrhein-Westfalen and Rheinland-Pfalz)

ledger.note: 911: Lotharingia turns to Charles the Simple. After Louis the Child died, the Lotharingian nobles 'declared Charles their new king, breaking from East Francia'; 'Charles the Simple was crowned King of Lotharingia in early November 911'. [fx-38 H51, 2026-11-01: the region is now the gazetteer region Lotharingia minus Cliopatria's Kingdom of Germany of 922 within Germany, as duchy-of-lotharingia ledger/0 draws it (703 cells less 158 = 545). The unmodified region booked 177 cells of East Frankish land (Westphalia east of the Rhine, Worms, Speyer, Koblenz) as Lotharingian. Lotharingia page: the region covered 'parts of modern Germany west of the Rhine'; 'In 925, Lotharingians under Gilbert elected Henry the Fowler to be their king'; Henry's 923 invasion 'invaded Lotharingia (including Alsace)'.]

922: Robert I, Odo's brother, is crowned by the rebels. 'Robert, who was Odo's brother, was elected king by the rebels and crowned' while Charles fled to Lotharingia; he dies at Soissons on 15 June 923. The Robertians hold the crown; the state continues.
923: Rudolph, Duke of Burgundy, is elected king after Robert I's death. The page's list gives his reign as 923-936. Charles the Simple is captured by Herbert II of Vermandois in summer 923.

minus.text: the East Frankish kingdom's own lands before 925 (Westphalia east of the Rhine, the Worms-Speyer-Mainz Rhine Franconia); its German cells only (the shape also covers 18 cells of Drenthe, Overijssel and Gelderland, which stay Lotharingian: 'the Netherlands')

region.text: Lotharingia including Alsace, less the East Frankish lands of 922 east of the Rhine (the gazetteer region Lotharingia is all of Nordrhein-Westfalen and Rheinland-Pfalz)

ledger.note: 923: Henry the Fowler invades Lotharingia. 'In 923, Henry the Fowler invaded Lotharingia (including Alsace)'; Charles, deposed in the west, 'remained king in Lotharingia'. The Treaty of Bonn between Charles and Henry was signed 7 November 921 (Charles the Simple page). [fx-38 H51, 2026-11-01: the region is now the gazetteer region Lotharingia minus Cliopatria's Kingdom of Germany of 922 within Germany, as duchy-of-lotharingia ledger/0 draws it (703 cells less 158 = 545). The unmodified region booked 177 cells of East Frankish land (Westphalia east of the Rhine, Worms, Speyer, Koblenz) as Lotharingian. Lotharingia page: the region covered 'parts of modern Germany west of the Rhine'; 'In 925, Lotharingians under Gilbert elected Henry the Fowler to be their king'; Henry's 923 invasion 'invaded Lotharingia (including Alsace)'.]

region.text: the Bessin, up to the river Vire

ledger.note: 924: King Rudolph extends Rollo's county westward. 'In 924, King Rudolph extended Rollo's county westward up to the river Vire, including the Bessin.' The page does not mention Maine or Le Mans. Cliopatria draws the addition in 926, two years later: 79 cells, of which 23 are in Calvados (the Bessin), 21 in Orne, 20 in Eure, 7 in Manche and 2 in Mayenne; this event takes the 23 Calvados cells (my reading) and the next one the rest.

region.text: Lotharingia including Alsace, less the East Frankish lands of 922 east of the Rhine (the gazetteer region Lotharingia is all of Nordrhein-Westfalen and Rheinland-Pfalz)

ledger.note: 925: the Lotharingians choose Henry. 'In 925, Lotharingians under Gilbert elected Henry the Fowler to be their king.' The Charles the Simple page: 'In 925, Lotharingia was once again seized by East Francia.' [fx-38 H51, 2026-11-01: the region is now the gazetteer region Lotharingia minus Cliopatria's Kingdom of Germany of 922 within Germany, as duchy-of-lotharingia ledger/0 draws it (703 cells less 158 = 545). The unmodified region booked 177 cells of East Frankish land (Westphalia east of the Rhine, Worms, Speyer, Koblenz) as Lotharingian. Lotharingia page: the region covered 'parts of modern Germany west of the Rhine'; 'In 925, Lotharingians under Gilbert elected Henry the Fowler to be their king'; Henry's 923 invasion 'invaded Lotharingia (including Alsace)'.]

region.text: Lotharingia, seized by East Francia, less the East Frankish lands of 922 east of the Rhine (the gazetteer region Lotharingia is all of Nordrhein-Westfalen and Rheinland-Pfalz)

ledger.note: 925: Lotharingia passes to East Francia (Henry the Fowler). Cliopatria's West Franks shape loses it in 926. [fx-38 H51, 2026-11-01: the region is now the gazetteer region Lotharingia minus Cliopatria's Kingdom of Germany of 922 within Germany, as duchy-of-lotharingia ledger/0 draws it (703 cells less 158 = 545). The unmodified region booked 177 cells of East Frankish land (Westphalia east of the Rhine, Worms, Speyer, Koblenz) as Lotharingian. Lotharingia page: the region covered 'parts of modern Germany west of the Rhine'; 'In 925, Lotharingians under Gilbert elected Henry the Fowler to be their king'; Henry's 923 invasion 'invaded Lotharingia (including Alsace)'.]

minus.text: the Cotentin and western Normandy added to Rollo's duchy

region.text: the other cells of Cliopatria's 926 addition to Normandy

ledger.note: 926: Cliopatria adds the other 56 cells (Orne 21, Eure 20, Manche 7, Mayenne 2, 6 elsewhere) to its Duchy of Normandy at West Francia's expense; no opened page names them. The Saint-Clair page says only that 'over subsequent decades, Rollo's successors expanded this domain westward to include the Cotentin'; the West Francia page that 'Dukes of Normandy refused to recognise Rudolf until 933'. The Duchy of Normandy page has the Avranchin and the Cotentin granted to William Longsword in 933 and 'forcibly taken from the Duchy of Brittany'; Cliopatria shows that only in 936 (22 cells, 19 in Manche, in its Brittany and Viking shapes and in no West Franks shape), so it is not a West Frankish loss.
936: Louis IV restores Carolingian rule. The page's list gives Louis IV 936-954; Hugh the Great 'was elevated to the title duke of the Franks by King Louis IV'. No border moves.

987: Hugh Capet is elected king and the Capetian dynasty begins. Infobox: 'Capetian dynasty established: June 987'; 'In 987 Hugh's son Hugh Capet was elected king' - 'traditionally marking the end of the French branch of Carolingian dynasty as well as the end of West Francia as a kingdom'. The state continues as the Kingdom of France (Cliopatria 990).

region.text: Aquitaine, the name the West Francia page uses ('Aquitania, Guyenne and Gascony' in the gazetteer)

ledger.note: 989: the dossier ends; Aquitaine's nominal homage is carried to the Kingdom of France dossier. The Duchy of Aquitaine page (opened 2026-10-24) dates no submission, recognition or end in 888-1000: it says only that a later duke, William IV, 'fought against Hugh Capet, king of France' (undated). Cliopatria's Duchy of Aquitaine begins in 990 with an allegiance to the Kingdom of France; the end here is that row's start, not a page.

region.text: the whole kingdom

ledger.note: 989: West Francia ends as the Kingdom of France begins in Cliopatria (990). The page names the Kingdom of France as the successor; the traditional end of West Francia is the Capetian election of June 987.

wars.name: Breton revolt and the Battle of Jengland

zones.text: the Breton marches (Rennes and Nantes side) that Cliopatria moves from the West Franks to Brittany in 860

wars.outcome: 'The Bretons were successful in obtaining a de facto independence' under Erispoë.

wars.name: Partition of Lothair II's kingdom (Treaty of Meerssen)
wars.outcome: Charles the Bald is crowned at Metz in 869; the partition of 8 August 870 gives him the west, Lyon and Vienne and part of Upper Burgundy including Besançon, and Louis the German the east with Aachen and Metz.

wars.name: Charles the Bald's invasion of East Francia

zones.text: Cliopatria's 876 addition from the East Franks (Rhine and Alsace side)

wars.outcome: Charles attacks after Louis the German's death (28 August 876) and is 'decisively beaten at the Battle of Andernach on 8 October 876'.

wars.name: Carolingian war against Boso
wars.outcome: Boso takes Lower Burgundy and Provence in 879; 'Boso suffered several territorial loses, but still kept his kingdom'; Vienne falls in September 882.
wars.note: Mâcon (March 880) and the sieges of Vienne are from the Boso page; the Ribemont page gives the war in general terms.

wars.name: Louis the Younger and the treaty of Ribemont

zones.text: western Lotharingia, which Cliopatria moves to the East Franks in 880

wars.outcome: Louis the Younger is invited to West Francia in 879 and, 'in February 880' at Ribemont, receives 'the western half of Lotharingia'; Louis III and Carloman II are recognised in the rest.

wars.name: Siege of Paris
wars.outcome: Sigfred's fleet sails up the Seine in 885; Charles the Fat camps at Montmartre in 886 and, when the Vikings withdraw, pays them '700 pounds of promised silver'. No border is drawn from it.

wars.name: Odo and Charles the Simple
wars.outcome: Fulk crowns the 14-year-old Charles at Reims in 893; Arnulf recognises him in 894 and returns to Odo in 895; in 896 Odo cedes part of the realm and makes Charles his successor; Odo dies 1 January 898.
wars.note: A civil war with no named territory; Charles held only Laon in 897 (Charles the Simple page).

wars.name: Rollo's settlement (Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte)
wars.outcome: Rollo is given the land west of the Epte, 'broadly Rouen and the area of present-day Upper Normandy', in return for baptism and vassalage; Dudo of Saint-Quentin, a century later, is the source of the terms.
wars.note: The page doubts the exact date and extent; the year 911 is 'likely in the autumn'.

wars.name: Charles the Simple, Henry the Fowler and Lotharingia
wars.outcome: Lotharingia switches to Charles in November 911; the Treaty of Bonn (7 November 921) recognises him; Henry invades in 923 and the Lotharingians elect him in 925.
wars.note: The Treaty of Bonn date is from the Charles the Simple page.

wars.name: Louis IV and Otto I over Lotharingia
wars.outcome: Gilbert's rebellion (936) and Louis IV's marriage to his widow keep a West Frankish claim alive; Otto defeats Gilbert at Andernach (939), accepts homage from Hugh the Great and Herbert II at Attigny (942) and meets a West Frankish invasion in 944 with a large army. No border moves.

wars.name: Lothair's Lotharingian war (Aachen and Paris)
wars.outcome: No border moved. In August 978 Lothair 'mounted an expedition into Lorraine' and sacked the imperial palace of Aachen; Otto II invaded West Francia in October 978 and lifted the siege of Paris on 30 November 978; at Margut-sur-Chiers in July 980 'Lothair renounced his rights to Lotharingia', which Cliopatria's West Franks shape of 980 does not hold. The Lotharingia page: 'In 978, king Lothair of West Francia invaded the region and captured Aachen, but Otto II ... counterattacked and reached the walls of Paris'; 'In 980, Lothair renounced his rights to Lotharingia.'

wars.name: Lothair's Verdun campaign
wars.outcome: No border moved on the page or in Cliopatria. After Otto II's death (7 December 983) Lothair, supported by Odo I of Blois and Herbert III of Meaux, 'invaded Upper Lotharingia, besieged Verdun and, by March of 985, had captured several important prisoners' (Godfrey I of Verdun, his son Frederick, Sigfried count of the Ardennes). The page gives no start date for the siege, dates the Peace of Worms ('reaffirmed the end of the Carolingian pretensions over Lotharingia') only after mid-984 and says Lothair never regained Lotharingia.

certainty.note: Borders are approximate: the Meerssen line of 870 ('ran roughly along the rivers Meuse, Ourthe, Moselle, Saone and Rhone') is the only described frontier, and Brittany, the Spanish March and Aquitaine are marches.

The East Frankish frontier fixed at Ribemont in 880 'remained largely the same until the Late Middle Ages' (Ribemont page) but is not described by lines; Aquitaine, Normandy, Brittany, Flanders and Burgundy are autonomous principalities with indefinite edges.

notes: Dates: the dossier starts at Verdun (August 843) and ends in 989, not at the Capetian election of June 987, so that the map has no gap before Cliopatria's Kingdom of France (990); 987 is a rename event. 843-849 overlaps Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks row (462-849). Cliopatria rows corrected: (1) 860-886 attach an Italian block of about 520-620 cells to the West Franks (Louis II's Kingdom of Italy, then Charles the Bald's brief Italian crown of 875-877 and Charles the Fat's from 879/880); removed. Cliopatria has no Kingdom of Italy shape for 845-886, so the kingdom-of-italy dossier (eu-13) should cover them. (2) 882-886 draw Charles the Fat's whole empire as West Francia; cut to West Francia, so the East Franks dossier (eu-07) must cover Germany and Austria in 882-886 (Cliopatria has no East Franks shape then). (3) 866-869 add Provence and the Rhône lands, 4 years before Meerssen, and 876-880 add 342 East Frankish cells from a defeated invasion; removed. (4) 922 adds 30 Breton cells; removed. (5) 936-959 remove the duchy of Burgundy; restored. (6) Aquitaine: Cliopatria's separate Aquitaine row (888-895) ends and its West Franks shape holds the land from 896. The first version subtracted that whole shape in 896-989, but it is all of southern France (Toulouse, Septimania, Gascony, Bordeaux, Auvergne), not only the duchy the page calls 'largely outside the control of the West Frankish kings', and no dossier owned the land; the corrections were reverted on 2026-10-24 (the Cliopatria shapes are used, with the 936 union with Upper Burgundy), and Aquitaine is a vassal (tint, region Aquitaine, counterpart duchy-of-aquitaine) from 889 to 989 inside the base shape, with a confidence-1 gain in 896 for the change of drawing. Small Cliopatria changes, dated in the second pass: the Breton-edge cells (Avranches and Coutances, 867, Salomon page), Urgell and Cerdanya (870) and Barcelona, Girona and Besalú (878) (Wilfred the Hairy page), Pallars and Ribagorza (872, County of Pallars page) and the Bessin (924, Duchy of Normandy page) are confidence 2; 56 Norman cells in 926 and the vassal end in 989 stay confidence 1. Not explained and left: 18 Gironde and Basque-coast cells added in 860 (West Frankish fill), 7 Alpine cells, 67 Frisian cells in 886 (cut by the 887 base of the 882-886 corrections) and a Septimania cell in 898. Corsica (33 cells) and the San Marino cell are removed with the Italian block in 860-880. 879 has its own keyframe (Boso's realm and Saône-et-Loire go to lower-burgundy). Lothair's wars of 978-980 and 985 are in wars (no border moved). Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-lotharingia (Lothair II, 855-869; Cliopatria draws it as 'Lower Burgundy' 860-869); Duchy of Burgundy before 1003 (Richard the Justiciar 880/918); Duchy of Aquitaine 896-989 (Cliopatria's Duchy of Aquitaine starts in 990); Lotharingia as duchy 911-959. Page budget: nine pages of its own (the West Francia page was opened twice with different questions) plus three opened for the Burgundy dossiers and cited where they date an event (Duchy of Burgundy, Boso of Provence, Louis the Blind). None failed. No page gives an area for West Francia, so Cliopatria's areas (322,000-1,188,000 km2; 354,000 in 960-989) could not be compared. Region names: Neustria, Septimania as a March, Marca Hispanica and Cambrai are not in the gazetteer; none is used.
